When the durable evidence courier is enabled, gateway operational posture MUST include `evidence_delivery`, carrying `pending`, `degraded` and `blocked`.
`pending` counts artifacts eligible for delivery or waiting for an active handoff.
Artifacts under a verified epoch or identity stop are excluded from `pending` and `blocked` and reported separately as stopped custody.
Stopped custody continues to degrade evidence health and reports `reprovisioning_required`.
It MAY carry `last_failure_at_ms` and `last_error` as a one-event diagnostic summary.

`last_error` is one of `channel_unavailable`, `channel_refused`, `channel_permanent_refusal`, `channel_receiver_state_refusal`, `malformed_channel_response`, `runtime_sink_unavailable`, `queue_retirement_failed`, `delivery_pending`, `channel_capacity_exhausted`, or `authority_retention_capacity_unavailable`, and `evidence_delivery` carries no other field than those this section names.
A terminal refusal, whether archived on a verified retention or held without one, is recorded as `channel_permanent_refusal`, and a `507 retention_capacity_exhausted` as `channel_capacity_exhausted`.
A `503 retention_capacity_unavailable` is recorded as `authority_retention_capacity_unavailable`, distinct from a generic `503`.
`last_error` is not the complete active-fault state, and a consumer MUST NOT infer clean delivery from its absence.
A degraded or blocked courier degrades the gateway and therefore the site.
Raw transport errors, endpoints, credentials, filesystem paths, and authority implementation identity MUST NOT appear in this projection.
A producer implementing this revision MUST carry `faults`, an array that is empty when no courier-level fault is active; an older producer MAY omit it.

Each entry is one of `store_unavailable`, `admission_failed`, `delivery_impaired`, `device_unconfigured`, `return_path_incompatible`, `reprovisioning_required`, or `stopped_custody_full`, and no entry repeats.
`store_unavailable` means the courier cannot read, write, or atomically update its durable store.
`admission_failed` means a valid artifact for a configured device could not complete admission: durable outbound queueing, and for a delivery envelope, durable staging of its required custody return.
It remains active until a later admission of the applicable form completes; a store probe never clears it.

`delivery_impaired` means the courier knows that one or more queued artifacts are held, waiting for a handoff, or backing off, but cannot enumerate every affected device and lane in `devices`; a producer that omits `devices` MUST raise it whenever it knows a non-clean per-device delivery state.
A present `devices` is complete, so a projection never carries both `delivery_impaired` and `devices`.
`device_unconfigured` means the gateway observed an outbound carriage for a device that is not configured, despite its configured topic ACLs; the projection never carries that device ID.
A broker-denied publication creates no gateway-side observation and so cannot raise it.
It clears only when that device becomes configured and a later valid handoff for it is admitted; elapsed time, silence, or a lost broker connection never clear it.

`return_path_incompatible` means the gateway keeps an authority artifact that a device's declared inbound carriage contract cannot carry, per *Return order is per device*; this revision's projection does not identify the device; the gateway's durable record of each kept artifact names it.
It clears only when no such artifact is kept.
`reprovisioning_required` means the gateway holds stopped custody: the device needs a new epoch under an epoch stop, or a replacement identity under an identity stop.
The `scope` of each `stopped_custody` entry says which; the runtime's `delivery_stop_status` says it for the runtime.
It is raised exactly when `stopped_custody` would be non-empty, and it clears only when no stopped custody is held.

`stopped_custody_full` means retained stopped custody has reached or exceeds a stopped-custody bound of [gateway-config/v2.md](../gateway-config/v2.md); it clears only when retained stopped custody is below every applicable bound.

With the courier enabled, each durable outbound and return store MUST be probed immediately after opening and then every `store_probe_interval_s`, independently of admissions and gateway-health publication.
`store_probe_interval_s` MUST be 300 through 900 seconds and defaults to 900.

A probe reads the store's directory and atomically replaces a fixed private probe file in that directory: it writes fresh bytes to a private temporary file, syncs it, renames it over the probe file, then syncs the directory.
It never creates, removes, rewrites, counts toward capacity, or reorders a queue record.
A failed probe, or any failed read, write, or atomic update of a store, raises `store_unavailable` for that store.
Only a successful probe of that store clears it; a later successful operation does not, so after a store recovers the fault can remain raised for up to one probe interval.
A probe never clears `admission_failed`.

Delivery to the evidence authority is ordered and held per device and lane ([evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md), refusal policy), so the projection MAY report it per device and lane in `devices`.
A producer that cannot enumerate durable per-device state omits it, and its omission conveys no per-device information: it is never evidence of clean delivery or an empty list.
When present, `devices` holds one entry for each device and lane whose delivery is not clean, and none for a lane whose delivery is clean:
| Field | Type and domain |

| `device_id` | the runtime node's own `device_id`, as in its carriage topic: 1 to 128 Unicode scalar values, none of them a control character (general category `Cc`), a character with the Unicode `White_Space` property, `/`, `+`, or `#`; no subordinate device identity is carried |
| `lane` | `registration` or `evidence`: the device's anchor registrations, or every other artifact it delivers |
| `pending` | integer, at least 1, that lane's artifacts counted in the gateway-level `pending`; never a stopped one |
| `state` | `held`, `waiting_handoff`, or `backing_off` |
| `held` | present exactly when `state` is `held` |
No two entries share a `device_id` and `lane`.
`held` describes the refused artifact at the head of that lane's order; its `artifact_type` is `anchor_registration` in the `registration` lane and never in the `evidence` lane:
| Field | Type and domain |
| `queue_record` | 64 lowercase hex, the durable queue record identifier |
| `artifact_digest` | `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex, over the artifact bytes |
| `artifact_type` | the closed outbound carriage vocabulary |
| `refusal_status` | the HTTP status that caused the hold |
| `reason` | a reason at which `refusal_status` holds in the evidence-transport refusal policy, or `unrecognised` |
| `first_held_at_ms` | integer, when the head was first refused, surviving restarts |
| `acknowledged` | boolean; `false` until an operator acknowledgement surface exists |

A terminal refusal the authority retained is archived rather than held, in either lane ([evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md), refusal policy), and the archive keeps incident metadata, never the bytes.
A producer implementing this revision MUST carry `incidents`, an array with one entry for each unacknowledged incident, and empty when there is none; an older producer MAY omit it.
This revision defines no `archived_registrations`: every archived refusal, in either lane, is a member of exactly one incident.
An archived refusal is never in `devices`, never counted in `pending`, and never makes `blocked` true:
| Field | Type and domain |
| `device_id` | as in `devices` |
| `anchor_epoch_id` | `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex, or `""` when the retention names none |
| `artifact_type` | the closed outbound carriage vocabulary |
| `refusal_status` | the HTTP status of the retained refusal |
| `reason` | a reason at which `refusal_status` archives in the evidence-transport refusal policy |
| `count` | integer, at least 1, the incident's distinct member digests |
| `first_refused_at_ms` | integer, when the first member was archived, surviving restarts |
| `last_refused_at_ms` | integer, at least `first_refused_at_ms`, when the latest member was archived |
| `first_digest` | `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex, the first member |
| `latest_digest` | as `first_digest`, the latest member; equal to `first_digest` exactly when `count` is 1 |

A producer implementing this revision MUST carry `stopped_custody`, an array with one entry for each device and lane that holds stopped custody, and empty when none does; an older producer MAY omit it.

A lane holds stopped custody when a verified `stop` projection ([evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md), stopped scopes) covers queued entries of it; they stay in custody, in order, and are never archived.
A stopped entry is never in `devices`, never counted in `pending`, and never makes `blocked` true:
| Field | Type and domain |
| `device_id` | as in `devices` |
| `lane` | as in `devices` |
| `scope` | `epoch` or `identity` |
| `count` | integer, at least 1, that lane's entries in stopped custody |
`scope` is required and is exactly `epoch` or `identity`, copied from the verified stop projection governing the stopped custody.
A lane whose entries a verified `identity` stop covers is governed by that stop, since it covers every entry of that device.
No two entries share a `device_id` and `lane`.
Stopped custody is bounded per identity and in total by the stopped-custody bounds of [gateway-config/v2.md](../gateway-config/v2.md), and no bound is ever met by eviction or deletion.

An artifact that would enter stopped custody beyond an applicable bound is not accepted into gateway custody: the gateway publishes no outbound acknowledgement and no custody acknowledgement for it, and the runtime keeps its bytes.

An entry already in gateway custody that a verified stop covers moves into stopped custody whatever the bound, because custody never moves backward, and the move raises `stopped_custody_full` when it reaches or passes a bound.
The retained stopped set stays readable and recoverable.
A courier that opens with retained stopped custody above a configured bound opens, raises `stopped_custody_full`, refuses additional stopped custody, and delivers every lane that is not stopped.

An incident coalesces the archived refusals that share `device_id`, `anchor_epoch_id`, `artifact_type`, `refusal_status` and `reason`; refusals that differ in any of them never coalesce, and no two entries share all five.
The gateway reads `anchor_epoch_id`, `refusal_status` and `reason` from the verified retention, never from the artifact.

It keeps, durably and for every incident, the digest of each distinct member, so every member stays enumerable and individually retrievable from the authority by digest, and `count` is the number of those digests.
Archiving a digest that is already a member, such as an identical retry or a re-offer of the same bytes, changes no field.
Timestamps are the gateway's clock at archive and survive restarts, as does every incident.

Acknowledgement changes alert visibility only: an acknowledged incident leaves `incidents` and stops degrading the gateway, and nothing else changes — its members, their retained bytes at the authority, and every evidence finding stay as they were.

A distinct member archived after acknowledgement reopens that incident: it returns to `incidents` unacknowledged, with `count`, `last_refused_at_ms` and `latest_digest` advanced and its first fields unchanged.
This revision defines no operator acknowledgement surface, so every incident stays unacknowledged until one exists.
`degraded` is true exactly when `faults` is non-empty, `devices` is present and non-empty, `incidents` is present and non-empty, or `stopped_custody` is present and non-empty.
When `faults`, `devices`, `incidents` and `stopped_custody` are all absent, `degraded` keeps an older producer's advisory meaning; their absence is unknown, never evidence of clean delivery.
`blocked` is true exactly when `pending` is positive, `devices` is present, every pending artifact is represented by `devices`, and every represented lane is held.
Stopped custody never makes `blocked` true, and a lane whose only queued entries are stopped has no entry in `devices`.
A fault never makes `blocked` true, and when `devices` is absent `blocked` is false.
A lane delivering cleanly has no entry in `devices`, so the entries' `pending` never sum to more than the gateway-level `pending`.
One held lane degrades the gateway and the site; it does not report the gateway blocked while another lane is still delivering.
Every field here is within the prohibition above: a digest identifies bytes, not an endpoint or a credential, and a reason or fault is drawn from a closed vocabulary.
A consumer that does not know `devices`, `faults` or `stopped_custody` ignores them.

[`vectors/site-health-evidence-delivery.json`](vectors/site-health-evidence-delivery.json) fixes accepted and refused projections, and `scripts/check-gateway-site-health-evidence-vectors` holds them to these rules.
MQTT PUBACK is not proof the gateway durably stored the bytes.
After an atomic queue commit or an explicit refusal for a configured device, the gateway publishes:
`artifact_digest` is SHA-256 over the decoded exact artifact bytes.
`outcome` is `queued` or `refused`.
`reason` is empty for `queued`; the closed transport refusal vocabulary is `malformed`, `binding_mismatch`, and `queue_full`.
`queue_full` is an acknowledgement only for a configured device whose reserved queue share cannot presently accept the artifact; it is retriable and MUST NOT be flattened into a drop.

For an authenticated admission, as [evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md) defines it — a carriage received on a configured device's own outbound topic under the broker posture the gateway asserts, whose topic, carriage and artifact `device_id` agree — a `queue_full` decision MUST signal the existing courier worker for that device after the refusal acknowledgement is published.
No durable record of a `queue_full` refusal exists.
It MUST NOT create a queue row, retire the offered artifact, bypass backoff, or imply custody.
The runtime retries an artifact refused `queue_full` with its existing bounded back-off.
An artifact larger than the evidence-transport maximum, 1,048,576 bytes, is refused `malformed` before custody, since no authority will accept it.
Queue capacity is reserved per device, so one device cannot exhaust another's.

Capacity and the configured devices are courier configuration, reserved equally per configured device; a gateway MUST reject an outbound-carriage topic whose device is not configured before invoking admission: it does not admit the artifact, issue custody, or publish an outbound acknowledgement, so an unconfigured device cannot consume an implicit shared lane, and the runtime keeps the bytes and retries.

The gateway MUST NOT refuse an artifact at admission because of its declared `v`; the evidence authority alone decides version support ([evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md), courier opacity).

A gateway implementing `gateway-api/v1` answers `malformed` for any `v` other than 1; that refusal is a statement about that gateway, not about the bytes, and only a `malformed` from a gateway claiming this contract is terminal for the artifact.

The acknowledgement uses the normal runtime-gateway envelope secret with `message_type` `evidence_outbound_ack`, empty `request_id`, the target `device_id`, and the usual canonical payload without `auth`.
It is an authenticated transport decision, not an evidence artifact and not an authority receipt.
**Two timestamps, two meanings.** `acknowledged_at_ms` is the queue decision time and repeats: re-admitting the same bytes recovers the same entry and the same decision.

`auth.signed_at_ms` is the gateway's signing time and MUST be strictly increasing across the acknowledgements one gateway issues — one millisecond past the previous when the clock has not moved, and durable across a gateway restart so an unchanged or regressed clock cannot reissue an earlier value — so two acknowledgements are never byte-identical.
A runtime's replay defence keys on the signature, and a re-acknowledgement that repeated the first would be refused as a replay rather than applied.
For `delivery_envelope`, a `queued` acknowledgement does not advance runtime custody state.
The gateway also sends the separately authenticated `custody_acknowledgement` through the inbound route below, and only that artifact can mark custody.
For the other outbound types, `queued` permits the runtime to retire its courier handoff copy because the gateway's durable queue now owns retry.
For `anchor_registration` it does not retire the runtime's durable epoch-confirmation obligation or its sealed re-offer bytes ([evidence-exchange/v2.md](../evidence-exchange/v2.md)).
An admission covered by a stop enters stopped custody only within the applicable bounds.
After the stopped bytes and their return obligation are durable, the gateway publishes `queued`.
For a `delivery_envelope`, it also durably stages and subsequently delivers the custody acknowledgement; that acknowledgement is what permits the runtime to release its local copy.
Beyond an applicable bound, the gateway accepts no custody and publishes neither acknowledgement.
The custody acknowledgement is staged durably before `queued` is published, so `queued` never leads the runtime to expect proof of custody that is not yet durable.

The stop is that of [evidence-transport/v2.md](../evidence-transport/v2.md), stopped scopes, and the bounds are those of [gateway-config/v2.md](../gateway-config/v2.md), as *Site Health `evidence_delivery` Projection* below states.
If an acknowledgement is lost, the runtime republishes the same carriage.
The gateway's queue is idempotent by `(artifact_type, artifact_digest)` and returns a newly signed acknowledgement.
A full queue never produces `queued` and never produces custody.
